title: Then the Code, Then Green
kicker: The smallest change that makes the table pass
html:
Then the Code, Then Green

data class LibraryPolicy(
    val renewalWeeks: Long = DEFAULT_RENEWAL_WEEKS,
) {
    companion object {
        const val DEFAULT_RENEWAL_WEEKS = 3L

        fun of(text: String): LibraryPolicy {
            val read = Properties().apply { load(text.reader()) }
            return LibraryPolicy(
                renewalWeeks = read.getProperty("renewal.weeks")
                    ?.trim()?.toLong() ?: DEFAULT_RENEWAL_WEEKS,
            )
        }
    }
}

One Rule

renewal.weeks, read from the library’s policy file. Left out: three weeks.

A Renewal Uses It

The due date moves by the policy’s weeks.

Green, Logged

All four rows pass, through the runner.

say: Only now does the code change, and the hook lets it, because a feature file changed first. Here's the heart of it, from the real commit. A policy, read from a properties file, with one rule: renewal.weeks. If the file leaves it out, three weeks. And a renewal now moves the due date by however many weeks the policy says. That's it. Then the suite runs again, through the runner, and all four rows pass. Green, logged.
